chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zureys, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding a man who set out as a pilgrim for the Hajj of Islam, and he died on the way, he said: If he died in the Sanctuary (Haram), the Hajj of Islam suffices for him; and if he died outside the Sanctuary, then his guardian should perform the Hajj of Islam on his behalf.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who dies during the Hajj journey?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the 'Hajj of Islam' (the obligatory first Hajj) and subsequent voluntary pilgrimages, emphasizing that the sanctity of the Haram boundaries validates the initial intention if death occurs there. It underscores the Shia legal principle that the heir bears the responsibility of fulfilling this specific debt of worship if the pilgrim died before reaching the sacred precincts. This distinction is crucial in Usuli fiqh for determining whether the obligation is personal and immediate or transferable to the estate.
